NGCC is integrated as part of @ngtools/webpack which is used in the Angular CLI.

Unless you have a custom build system and not using any of the above, you need to run NGCC as a post install hook.

If opting out of ivy is not working, ie a build which used to work is no longer working, we’d need to take a look at it.

Which version of the framework are you using?

@kemsky > * If you disable Ivy and try to build as usual with regular `ngc` - it fails and you have to remove node_modules and install again. As part of running ngcc, existing code in `node_modules` is AOT compiled into Ivy instructions. If you run ngcc using its executable `ivy-ngcc` then this step overwrites library files in-place, with a backup file suffixed with `.bak` being produced as well. Besides the generation of Ivy code, the original Angular decorators such as `@Component` and `@Input` etc. are removed from the code, as Ivy conveys such metadata in a different, tree-shakeable way. Therefore, the `node_modules` directory has then been modified in a way that it can no longer be used when disabling Ivy, as vital information is no longer present in the library files. The same is not true when using the Angular CLI, as its execution of ngcc under the covers will use a different approach that does not suffer from the same problem: instead of overwriting files in-place, a dedicated `__ivy_ngcc__` subdirectory is created in each library that gets compiled for Ivy. The CLI will then redirect Webpack to use the sources from the subdirectory, instead of the non-Ivy code originally shipped to NPM. Hence, this way disabling Ivy should not see the need to reinstall `node_modules`. > * I received a lot of strange compiler errors: > > ``` > __ng_typecheck__.ts:13549:11 - error TS2339: Property 'caption' does not exist on type 'HTMLDivElement'. > > 13549 _t132.caption = "Defendant 4 Is Covered: "; > ``` > Corresponding template: > > ``` >
> ``` > > Code: > > ```ts > export abstract class AbstractFormComponent extends AbstractComponent implements ControlValueAccessor, IFocusContainer { > ... > @Input('caption') > public label:string; > ... > } > ``` > > Looks like alias is ignored... Thanks for sharing this! The type checking of Angular template code has been completely redesigned to be far more extensive than the type checking that was done previously. It should be able to catch many more bugs that were previously not discovered. In this case however, I don't have enough insight to see if this is a false-positive in the new type-checker, of if there's legitimately reason to believe there's a type error somewhere. By the looks of it, a concrete directive/component of `AbstractFormComponent` could not be matched (leaving the property left-over for the `div` element) *or* it could not be statically determined that the parent class of the matched directive/component is `AbstractFormComponent`, which also *currently* results in applying the property to the `div` element. If you think neither of the above is the case, there may indeed be buggy behavior with either class hierarchies (which _should_ be supported *iff* the class hierarchy can be statically determined) *or* with the aliased input (which _should_ also be taken into account already). Would you be able to provide a minimal reproduction of this issue, so that we can look into what is causing it? > > Also I'd like to know is ivy-ngcc documented anywhere? I need to skip processing of certain modules. It doesn't currently have a lot of documentation. May I ask, why do you need to skip processing of certain libraries? Are they Angular libraries that are processed but you think they shouldn't?
